faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a metal roof on a Montclair home?

runs.v: A re-roof of the covering on a detached one- or two-family home counts as ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 with no construction permit. A commercial, multi-family, or attached building needs a permit once roof work exceeds 25% of the roof area in 12 months, as does any structural change; about 19% of Montclair homes sit in two- to four-unit buildings and about 14% in buildings of 20 or more units (U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2019-2023), so confirm with the Montclair construction office, since installation requests often require a building permit and compliance certification.

faqs.q: Is metal the right roof for a Montclair Victorian or Tudor?

runs.v: Copper and standing seam suit a Montclair home's roof where the original detailing used metal, such as turret caps, mansard sections, and dormer faces, while natural slate suits the broad slopes.

faqs.q: Should I repair or replace a Montclair metal roof?
